Affected baseline scope: 25 of 26 baseline items are listed in the packet: 1–10 and 12–26; audit item 11 is not affected.

Reconciliation counts: 26 reconciled and 26 unique; exact_match/accurately_unavailable 5, missing_from_source/mismatch 2, exact_match/mismatch 14, variant_match/mismatch 1, normalized_match/mismatch 3, and missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable 1.

The official site identifies four distinct service contexts—Pier, Wine Bar, brunch, and Wine Bar Happy Hour—but its main menu widget exposes only “Loading Menu” to the accessible source. It cannot establish a complete current catalog.
OpenTable supplies detailed item descriptions, but it remains third-party evidence and cannot be promoted to restaurant-issued ingredient authority.
The official FAQ only states that V and G options are marked on menus. It does not provide complete allergen arrays, allergen negatives, shared-equipment information, or a cross-contact policy.
The incomplete restaurant-issued surfaces cannot support baseline-only removals, complete allergen arrays, allergen negatives, or cross-contact conclusions.

The official homepage does support narrow positives where explicit: Soft Scramble explicitly contains eggs; Torrijas explicitly includes whipped labneh, supporting milk; and Serrano Ham Croquetas is explicitly topped with manchego, supporting milk.

The core deterministic gates for multi-service scope, count drift, current-only/baseline-only uncertainty, non-exact reconciliation, allergen-authority mismatch, unresolved cross-contact, validation warnings, and low confidence remain materially justified.

Terra understated the official Wine Bar Happy Hour content: the current restaurant-issued homepage explicitly names Tzatziki with warm bread, Chickpea Hummus, Patatas Bravas, Butternut Squash Skordalia, Marinated Cucumbers, and Serrano Ham Croquetas with manchego. The surface remains partial, but these positive mentions must not be erased.
Terra over-promoted egg for Torrijas from the culinary identity “French toast.” The official text explicitly supports milk through labneh, but does not explicitly disclose egg.
Terra over-promoted wheat for Soft Scramble from the generic word “toast.” The official text explicitly supports egg, but toast alone does not establish wheat.

Terra’s wheat finding for Garlic Chicken Montadito relies on culinary-name interpretation; the cited OpenTable description explicitly lists Mahón cheese but not bread. Milk is supported, while wheat is not established by that description alone.
Terra’s egg finding for flan and wheat finding for shortbread depend on culinary assumptions rather than explicit listed ingredients. Such assumptions cannot be promoted as disclosed allergens.

The inaccessible-source gate should not be interpreted as proving every official surface inaccessible: the homepage and FAQ are accessible, while the embedded primary menu enumeration and attempted ordering page are unavailable. The narrower gate remains valid.

The duplicate-presentations gate is not independently proven by service multiplicity alone. Distinct Pier and Wine Bar services do not themselves establish duplicate item presentations; the packet’s duplicate-presentation count should remain an upstream reconciliation concern rather than a source-confirmed fact.
